pr.title: Say whether an upgrade changed what project init writes
pr.head: c37c90879ef22863e0b2b4928b74eb9ff9115c32

summary: project upgrade reinstalls the project command and the host plugins by running Projector's installer, install.sh, and passes on the installer's output and exit status. project init is the separate command that writes Projector's generated files: the Projector section in a repository's AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, the site workflow .github/workflows/projector-site.yml, and the permission rules in your Claude Code settings and Codex rules. Until now, nothing told you whether a new release changed any of those, so you either ran init in every repository after each upgrade or waited for project check to warn. check never reports the permission rules at all.

This pull request makes upgrade answer that question. It takes a SHA-256 digest of each of the three outputs before the installer runs. After the install, it asks the project on PATH for the same digests through a new hidden flag, project version --init-digests. It then prints rows in the installer's own two-column format:

• init-changed, once for each output whose digest differs, followed by a yellow init-needed row that says to run project init.
  • init-current when nothing changed.
  • init-unknown when the project on PATH cannot answer, because it predates the flag or is missing.

The exit status stays the installer's. After a failed install, upgrade still lists what changed, because a failed all install can already have replaced the CLI. It prints no init-current or init-unknown row in that case. upgrade never writes a repository or settings file itself. You run init when the rows ask for it.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Digest: a SHA-256 hash of what init would write, with a label that names the output. The instructions and the workflow are rendered for one fixed repository, docs/projects and action ref v0, which is enough to show a template change.
  • The project on PATH: the command you run init with next, and the one the installer's cli row reports on. The running process still holds the old code, so upgrade asks this command for the new digests.
  • Installer row: a line of install.sh output, a name padded to 14 columns and then the text. A warning row adds ⚠️ and prints bold yellow on a terminal unless NO_COLOR is set.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The Projector review of c37c908 was clean, with no finding threads and two suggestions.
  • The review ran upgrade end to end against a stub installer with a temporary home, covering each changed output, an unchanged install, an older or missing project, failed installs, an unreachable installer, and a checkout install. It found that no repository or settings file changed.
  • The first upgrade that prints these rows is one run from a release that includes this change, because the comparison runs in the command being replaced.

groups.title: Upgrade compares what init writes before and after the install
groups.kicker: The digests, the hidden flag, and the rows that report them
intro: run_upgrade now has three steps. It takes init_digests() from the running code, runs the installer through run_installer, which is the old run_upgrade body, and calls report_init_changes. The order matters, because install.sh cli rewrites this package under the running interpreter, templates included.

installed_init_digests runs project version --init-digests from PATH with a 30-second timeout, and returns None on any failure or malformed answer. report_init_changes compares by name and digest, and prints the newer command's label. So a newer release can name an output this command has never heard of, and an output that the newer release stopped writing is not reported.

checks.text: The review recomputed the three digests by hand, from the template with docs/projects substituted, from json.dumps of ALLOW, ASK, SUPERSEDED, RETIRED_ASK, and CODEX_RULES, and from workflow_text("v0"). Each matched the hidden flag's output.

The digests cover every file init rewrites. init creates the projects README once and never rewrites it, so it is rightly left out. The CLAUDE.md import line, @AGENTS.md, is a constant that no digest covers.

files.note: Adds init_digests, installed_init_digests, installer_row, and report_init_changes. It splits run_upgrade into the installer run and the report, and adds the hidden version --init-digests flag.

checks.text: The digests are taken before the installer runs. In an end-to-end run, a stub installer rewrote the running package's own template in place, as a pipx reinstall does, and upgrade still reported the changed Projector section.
An older project on PATH and a PATH with no project each printed init-unknown after a successful install. After a failed one, each printed no row and kept the installer's exit status.

init-unknown tells you to run project check, which warns about the Projector section and the site workflow but not about the permission rules. project review rules reports those. The review lists this as a suggestion.
project help version doesn't show the hidden flag, and the flag's JSON answer works from an uninstalled checkout, whose version is unknown.

groups.title: Tests for each row and for the digests
intro: UpgradeTests now patches installed_init_digests by default to return the running command's own digests, so every existing upgrade test expects init-current unless it says otherwise. The new tests cover each row, the order of the digests and the installer, a separate digest for each output, and a real project on PATH that answers or refuses the flag.

files.note: Seven new tests in UpgradeTests, plus a default patch in setUp.

checks.text: The full suite passed at this head: 1,140 tests, 1 skipped, with python3.12.
